text.p: Financial services group Mercantile Mutual said on Monday it was targeting at least a ten percent after-tax profit growth in 1996/97.
Mercantile said earlier it achieved an 18 percent rise in net profit to A$71.1 million in the 1995/96 year ended September 30, with group assets under management rising 38 percent to A$11.9 billion.

Asked if the company expected to achieve the same profit growth in percentage terms this financial year, he said: "that's probably a little bolder than we would make in a forecast...(we are looking at) at least ten percent increase."

"Everything we can control in an operational sense, we are confident about," managing director Rod Atfield told Reuters, saying one variable was the treatment of unrealised gains from general insurance activity as required by Australian accounting standards.

Atfield said the group was quite bullish about its prospects, its only reservation being a concern that the the United States share market was a bit overheated and this could negatively affect the local market.
Mercantile Mutual is a unit of Dutch insurance and banking group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV.

Atfield said Mercantile, which has recently acquired Pacific Mutual Australia Ltd, and the Bleakleys financial planning group, was looking at further acquisitions in fund management and life and general insurance.
It has already signalled its interest in the New South Wales state-owned Axiom funds management group, the sale of which is expected to be completed in early 1997.
"In the medium term, we are examining quite a number," he said but declined to detail any prospects other than to say any acquisition would have to be substantial.
